nature-found-023.q: What share of Earth's land did a 2021 study find ecologically and faunally intact?

nature-found-003.q: Why do lower latitudes generally hold more species than higher latitudes?
nature-found-003.a: Several factors may contribute, but the underlying one behind many of them is the higher average temperature at the equator.

nature-found-013.q: When was the SEEA Central Framework for environmental-economic accounts published in its final form?

nature-found-091.q: How is the assimilative capacity of a water body understood, using an irrigation standard for salt as an example?
nature-found-091.a: It is the amount of salt that can be added before the standard is passed; beyond that point a pollutant actually causes pollution.

nature-found-093.q: In the Review's model of households and the biosphere, what can a household's income divided by its efficiency be read as?

nature-found-092.q: Since the Neolithic Revolution, by about how much has human consumption cut the world's forest cover?

nature-found-032.q: What follows when social costs exceed private costs and people rely on private markets alone?

nature-found-040.q: How can the use values of natural assets be read from behaviour?
nature-found-040.a: From things like the cost of recreational trips or house prices, as in hedonic methods.

nature-found-050.q: What did Malthus argue in his 1798 Essay on the Principle of Population?
nature-found-050.a: That more food raises well-being only for a while, because population then grows.

nature-found-038.q: Why can future generations not influence today's market prices?
nature-found-038.a: Because they are not yet born, so they cannot influence prices at all.

nature-found-041.q: How much damage to nature have harmful subsidies conservatively been estimated to cause each year?
nature-found-041.a: Between $4 and $6 trillion U.S. dollars per year.

nature-found-048.a: Scarcity that arises when demand for a resource rises while supply stays the same.

nature-found-103.q: What do critics mean by policy myopia?
nature-found-103.a: That politicians favour quick, visible fixes over lasting long-term solutions.

nature-found-066.q: Why can subsidies waste scarce resources?
nature-found-066.a: Because they can shield inefficient firms from market forces.

nature-found-057.q: How many deaths did the 2024 Global Burden of Disease Study link to air pollution in 2021?
nature-found-057.a: It estimated pollution contributed to 8.1 million deaths, more than 1 in 8 deaths.

nature-found-099.q: What led to the building of London's sewer system?
nature-found-099.a: The Great Stink on the Thames in 1858.

nature-found-080.q: What does a corrective tax proportional to marginal damages yield?
nature-found-080.a: The efficient level of pollution reduction.

nature-found-104.q: What global economic loss did one study estimate from a 1% rise in ozone concentrations?
nature-found-104.a: A loss of $10 billion each year.

nature-found-078.q: Above what noise level can long exposure cause hearing loss?

nature-found-070.q: What did the US Noise Control Act of 1972 set?
nature-found-070.a: A national policy against noise that endangers health and welfare.

nature-found-105.q: What three kinds of sound do soundscapes combine?
nature-found-105.a: Biophony from organisms, geophony from natural non-biological sources and anthropophony from humans.

nature-econ-134.q: Why is biodiversity increasingly seen as having economic value?
nature-econ-134.a: Because of ecosystem services such as clean air, food, water, flood defence and pollination.

nature-econ-152.q: What makes a preference order rational?
nature-econ-152.a: It is both transitive and complete; people who follow one are called rational agents.

nature-econ-139.q: Who first introduced the concept of ordinal utility, and when?

nature-econ-115.q: What did Paul Samuelson argue answers all three basic economic questions at once in competitive markets?

nature-econ-113.q: What does the law of diminishing marginal productivity say?
nature-econ-113.a: That past some point each extra unit of input yields less output.

nature-econ-154.q: Which countries have large state-owned enterprise sectors alongside large private sectors, as mixed economies?

nature-econ-106.q: On a production possibilities frontier, what does a slope of 2 mean for producing one more packet of butter?

nature-econ-114.a: The extra cost of producing one more unit of output.

nature-econ-136.q: In one study of sunk-cost behaviour, how did managers told they had made the earlier poor investment behave?
nature-econ-136.a: They put in an average of $12.97 million more, versus $9.43 million for those told someone else had made it.

nature-econ-389.a: An exchange of goods or services, with or without money.

nature-econ-369.q: What does the value of a statistical life try to estimate?
nature-econ-369.a: How much people would pay to lower their risk of dying; it is used to cost deaths from air pollution.
